title: Ask him and tell me
scope: The conjunctive participle (stem + कर, करना करके, colloquial stem + के) linking actions, independent of ने, and as adverbs (दौड़कर, जान-बूझकर, कृपा करके, को छोड़कर, से होकर, भूलकर भी); telling the time with बजना (एक बजा है, दो बजे हैं, सवा, साढ़े, पौने, पौन, डेढ़, ढाई, बजकर, बजने में, बज रहे हैं, बजनेवाले हैं, पहर); सकना, पाना, चुकना after a stem, without ने; compound verbs with जाना, लेना, देना and the ने rule for them; verbs in combination (लौट आना, ले जाना, निकल आना, चला जाना); कि “or”

vocab.en: to go away, go one's way
(after a verb stem) to have already done
(after a verb stem) to manage to
(after a verb stem) to be able
one and a quarter, plus a quarter

lessons.title: जाकर, खाकर, करके
lessons.desc: The conjunctive participle: “having gone, after eating”

items.q: Fill the gap: “After bathing Raj will have breakfast.”
items.say: राज नहाकर नाश्ता करेगा ।
wrong: नहाता
नहाता is the imperfective participle, “bathing (habitually)”. A first action linked to the main verb is stem + कर.
नहाया
नहाया is the perfective, “bathed”. Hindi does not join two verbs this way. The first action is stem + कर.
नहानाकर
Not a word. कर goes on the bare stem, not on the infinitive: नहाकर.
items.why: The conjunctive participle is the verb stem + कर (नहाकर “having bathed”, “after bathing”). It links a first action to the main verb.

items.q: Fill the gap: “We will phone you after reaching Delhi.”
items.say: हम दिल्ली पहुँचकर तुम्हें फ़ोन करेंगे ।
wrong: पहुँचे
पहुँचे is the perfective or the subjunctive. The first of two actions is stem + कर.
पहुँचना
पहुँचना is the infinitive. The conjunctive participle is the stem + कर.
items.why: The conjunctive participle is the verb stem + कर (नहाकर “having bathed”, “after bathing”). It links a first action to the main verb.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Mohan got the luggage ready and went to the station.”
items.say: मोहन सामान तैयार करके स्टेशन गया ।
items.en: Mohan[0] got[3] the luggage[1] ready[2] and went[5] to the station[4].
wrong: करकर
Not a word. करना is the exception: its conjunctive participle is करके only.
किया
किया is the perfective, “did”. The first action takes the conjunctive participle.
कियाकर
Not a word. कर never goes on the perfective participle, and करना has करके.
items.why: करना is the exception: its conjunctive participle is करके only.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Sita went to the market and bought a sari.”
items.hi: सीता ने बाज़ार ___ एक साड़ी ख़रीदी ।
items.say: सीता ने बाज़ार जाकर एक साड़ी ख़रीदी ।
items.en: Sita[0] went[3] to the market[2] and bought[6] a[4] sari[5].
wrong: जानाकर
Not a word. कर goes on the bare stem, not on the infinitive: जाकर.
गयाकर
Not a word. कर goes on the bare stem, not on the perfective: जाकर.
गई
गई is the perfective. Hindi does not string two finite verbs together like this. The first action is जाकर.
items.why: The conjunctive participle is the verb stem + कर (नहाकर “having bathed”, “after bathing”). It links a first action to the main verb. The main verb ख़रीदना still takes ने, सीता ने.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Pinki drank her milk and went to sleep.”
items.say: पिंकी दूध पीकर सो गई ।
items.en: Pinki[0] drank[2] {her milk}[1] and {went to sleep}[3+4].
wrong: पिंकी ने
The main verb सो जाना is intransitive, so there is no ने, even though पीकर has an object.
पिंकी को
को does not mark the subject of सो जाना. The subject stays in the plain form.
items.why: The conjunctive participle does not affect the main clause: whether the doer takes ने depends only on the main verb.

items.q: Fill the gap: “The children went out running.”
items.say: बच्चे दौड़कर बाहर गए ।
wrong: दौड़ना
दौड़ना is the infinitive. The manner of the main action is stem + कर.
दौड़ा
दौड़ा is the perfective, “ran”, and it is singular. The manner of the main action is stem + कर.
दौड़नाकर
Not a word. कर goes on the bare stem: दौड़कर.
items.why: Some conjunctive participles work as adverbs of manner: दौड़कर “running”, हँसकर “laughingly”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “He broke my glass deliberately.”
items.say: उसने जान-बूझकर मेरा गिलास तोड़ा ।
wrong: छोड़कर
छोड़कर “apart from” follows a noun with को (राज को छोड़कर).
होकर
होकर “via” follows the name of a place (लखनऊ से होकर).
items.why: जान-बूझकर “deliberately” is built on two conjunctive participles.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Everyone came except Raj.”
items.say: राज को छोड़कर सब लोग आए ।
wrong: होकर
होकर means “via”, of a route.
भूलकर
राज को भूलकर would mean “having forgotten Raj”, and भूलकर भी is “even by mistake”. “Except” is को छोड़कर.
items.why: X को छोड़कर “apart from X, except X”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “We went to Banaras via Lucknow.”
items.say: हम लखनऊ से होकर बनारस गए ।
items.en: We[0] went[5] to Banaras[4] via[2+3] Lucknow[1].
wrong: होता
होता is the imperfective participle of होना. “Via” is (से) होकर.
छोड़कर
छोड़कर “except” follows को, not a route.
items.why: (से) होकर “via”: लखनऊ से होकर “via Lucknow”.

items.q: Join the two sentences with a conjunctive participle
items.a: मोहन ने घर लौटकर अख़बार पढ़ा ।
wrong: मोहन घर लौटकर अख़बार पढ़ा ।
पढ़ना is transitive and the main verb is perfective, so the doer takes ने. लौटकर does not change that.
मोहन ने घर लौटा अख़बार पढ़ा ।
लौटा is the perfective. The first action goes into the conjunctive participle, लौटकर.
items.why: The conjunctive participle does not affect the main clause: whether the doer takes ने depends only on the main verb.
items.hi: मोहन घर लौटा । उसने अख़बार पढ़ा ।
items.say: मोहन ने घर लौटकर अख़बार पढ़ा ।
items.en: Mohan[0] returned[3] home[2] and read[5] the newspaper[4].

items.q: Use a conjunctive participle instead of “… के बाद”
wrong: खाना खाकर हमने बाज़ार गए ।
जाना is intransitive, so हम takes no ने. खाकर does not change that.
खाना खाता हम बाज़ार गए ।
खाता is the imperfective participle. Use stem + कर, खाकर.
खाना खानाकर हम बाज़ार गए ।
खानाकर is not a word. कर goes on the bare stem: खाकर.
items.why: The conjunctive participle is the verb stem + कर (नहाकर “having bathed”, “after bathing”). It links a first action to the main verb.
items.hi: खाना खाने के बाद हम बाज़ार गए ।
items.say: खाना खाकर हम बाज़ार गए ।
items.en: {After a meal}[0+1] we[2] went[4] to the market[3].

items.q: Fill the gap: “Please speak in a low voice.”
items.say: कृपा करके धीमी आवाज़ में बोलिए ।
wrong: कीजिए
कीजिए is the polite imperative. “Kindly” is the fixed phrase कृपा करके.
करकर
Not a word. करना is the exception: its conjunctive participle is करके only.
items.why: कृपा करके and मेहरबानी करके “kindly, please” are conjunctive participles of करना.

lessons.title: कितने बजे हैं ?
lessons.desc: Telling the time: बजा, बजे, सवा, साढ़े, पौने, बजकर, बजने में

items.q: Fill the gap: “Is it one o'clock?”
items.say: क्या एक बजा है ?
wrong: बजे
बजे is plural, used from two o'clock upwards (दो बजे हैं). One o'clock is singular.
बजता
बजता is the imperfective, “strikes (regularly)”. Telling the time uses the perfective बजा.
items.why: Telling the time: एक बजा है, but दो बजे हैं and upwards. “At” a time is the oblique बजे, even for one o'clock.

items.q: Fill the gap: “It's half past four.”
items.say: साढ़े चार बजे हैं ।
wrong: बजा
बजा goes with one o'clock (एक बजा है). साढ़े चार is plural.
बजकर
बजकर adds minutes past the hour (चार बजकर दस मिनट).
items.why: Telling the time: एक बजा है, but दो बजे हैं and upwards. “At” a time is the oblique बजे, even for one o'clock.

items.q: How do you say “The film will start at half past one”?
wrong: फ़िल्म साढ़े एक बजे शुरू होगी ।
The book uses साढ़े from three upwards. Half past one is डेढ़, “one and a half”.
फ़िल्म सवा बजे शुरू होगी ।
सवा बजे is at a quarter past one.
items.why: सवा “plus a quarter”, साढ़े “plus a half” (from three upwards), पौने “less a quarter”. 1.30 is डेढ़, 2.30 is ढाई.
items.say: फ़िल्म डेढ़ बजे शुरू होगी ।

items.q: Fill the gap: “Our bus will leave at half past two.”
items.say: हमारी बस ढाई बजे चलेगी ।
items.en: Our[0] bus[1] {will leave}[4] at[3] {half past two}[2].
wrong: डेढ़
डेढ़ बजे is at half past one.
सवा दो
सवा दो is a quarter past two.
items.why: सवा “plus a quarter”, साढ़े “plus a half” (from three upwards), पौने “less a quarter”. 1.30 is डेढ़, 2.30 is ढाई.

items.q: Fill the gap: “I get up at a quarter to seven every day.”
items.hi: मैं हर दिन ___ सात बजे उठता हूँ ।
items.say: मैं हर दिन पौने सात बजे उठता हूँ ।
items.en: I[0] {get up}[6+7] at[5] {a quarter to}[3] seven[4] every[1] day[2].
wrong: पौन
पौन “three-quarters” is used alone for a quarter to one (पौन बजा). Before an hour it is पौने.
सवा
सवा सात is a quarter past seven.
items.why: सवा “plus a quarter”, साढ़े “plus a half” (from three upwards), पौने “less a quarter”. 1.30 is डेढ़, 2.30 is ढाई.

items.q: Fill the gap: “It's twenty minutes to four.”
items.say: चार बजने में बीस मिनट हैं ।
wrong: बजकर
बजकर gives minutes past the hour. Minutes to the hour use बजने में.
बजे
बजे is not used here. Minutes to the hour use the oblique infinitive, बजने में.
items.why: Minutes past the hour use बजकर (दो बजकर दस मिनट), minutes to the hour use बजने में (दो बजने में दस मिनट).

items.q: Fill the gap: “The guests arrived at twenty-five minutes past three.”
items.hi: मेहमान तीन ___ पच्चीस मिनट पर पहुँचे ।
items.say: मेहमान तीन बजकर पच्चीस मिनट पर पहुँचे ।
items.en: {The guests}[0] arrived[6] at[5] twenty-five[3] minutes[4] past[2] three[1].
wrong: बजने में
तीन बजने में पच्चीस मिनट is twenty-five to three.
बजे
बजे cannot take minutes after it. Minutes past the hour use बजकर.
बजेकर
Not a word. कर goes on the bare stem of बजना, बजकर.
items.why: Minutes past the hour use बजकर (दो बजकर दस मिनट), minutes to the hour use बजने में (दो बजने में दस मिनट).

items.q: Fill the gap: “Meet me at one tomorrow.”
items.say: कल एक बजे मुझसे मिलो ।
wrong: बजा
बजा is used in telling the time (एक बजा है). “At” a time takes the oblique बजे, even for one o'clock.
बजकर
बजकर adds minutes past the hour (एक बजकर दस मिनट).
items.why: Telling the time: एक बजा है, but दो बजे हैं and upwards. “At” a time is the oblique बजे, even for one o'clock.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Hurry up, it's just striking five!”
items.say: जल्दी करो, पाँच बज रहे हैं !
wrong: रहा
रहा is singular. पाँच takes the plural, बज रहे हैं.
रही
रही is feminine. The time is told with masculine forms.
items.why: The continuous of बजना, बज रहे हैं, gives “it's just … o'clock”.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
wrong: It's half past twelve.
That would be साढ़े बारह बजे हैं. बजनेवाले हैं means “about to strike”.
It's ten past twelve.
That would be बारह बजकर दस मिनट हैं. Infinitive + वाला means “about to”.
items.why: बजनेवाले हैं — “(the hour) is about to strike”.

items.q: What does तीसरे पहर mean?
wrong: all day long
That is आठों पहर, “all eight watches”.
at three o'clock
पहर is a watch of about three hours, not an hour. Three o'clock is तीन बजे.
items.why: पहर is one of the eight three-hour watches of the traditional day. It survives in दोपहर, तीसरे पहर and आठों पहर.

items.q: Fill the gap: “The children reached school at a quarter past nine.”
items.say: बच्चे सवा नौ बजे स्कूल पहुँचे ।
items.en: {The children}[0] reached[5] school[4] at[3] {a quarter past}[1] nine[2].
wrong: साढ़े
साढ़े नौ is half past nine.
पौने
पौने नौ is a quarter to nine.
items.why: सवा “plus a quarter”, साढ़े “plus a half” (from three upwards), पौने “less a quarter”. 1.30 is डेढ़, 2.30 is ढाई.

items.q: Fill the gap: “I can't come this evening. (a man speaking)”
items.hi: मैं आज शाम को नहीं आ ___ ।
items.say: मैं आज शाम को नहीं आ सकता ।
items.en: I[0] can't[4+6] come[5] {this evening}[1+2+3]. (a man speaking)
wrong: सकती
सकती is feminine. The speaker is a man.
सकूँ
सकूँ is the subjunctive, “that I may be able”. A plain statement “I can't” is सकता.
items.why: सकना follows the bare stem: आ सकता “can come”. In the negative the auxiliary हूँ is usually dropped.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Sita couldn't read that letter.”
items.say: सीता वह चिट्ठी नहीं पढ़ सकी ।
wrong: सीता ने
सकना never takes ने, even after a transitive stem like पढ़.
सीता को
को does not mark the subject of सकना. The subject stays in the plain form.
items.why: सकना “can”, पाना “manage to” and चुकना “have already” follow the bare stem of another verb, agree with the subject and never take ने.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Can you come to the market with me tomorrow? (to a woman)”
items.hi: क्या तुम कल मेरे साथ बाज़ार चल ___ हो ?
items.say: क्या तुम कल मेरे साथ बाज़ार चल सकती हो ?
items.en: Can[7+8] you[1] come[6] to the market[5] with[4] me[3] tomorrow[2]? (to a woman)
wrong: सकते
सकते is masculine. The cue is to a woman.
सकतीं
With an auxiliary the feminine plural nasal goes on the last word only, and तुम … हो needs none: सकती हो.
items.why: सकना “can”, पाना “manage to” and चुकना “have already” follow the bare stem of another verb, agree with the subject and never take ने.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Raj won't be able to get to the office tomorrow.”
items.say: राज कल दफ़्तर नहीं पहुँच सकेगा ।
items.en: Raj[0] {won't be able to}[3+5] get[4] to the office[2] tomorrow[1].
wrong: सकेगी
सकेगी is feminine. Raj is a man.
सकेंगे
सकेंगे is plural. Raj, spoken of plainly, takes the singular.
items.why: सकना has a future: सकेगा, सकेगी, सकेंगे “will be able”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “The children didn't manage to hear the whole story.”
items.say: बच्चे पूरी कहानी नहीं सुन पाए ।
items.en: {The children}[0] {didn't manage to}[3+5] hear[4] the whole[1] story[2].
wrong: पाया
पाया is singular. बच्चे is plural.
पाईं
पाईं is feminine plural, as if agreeing with कहानी. पाना agrees with the subject, बच्चे.
items.why: सकना “can”, पाना “manage to” and चुकना “have already” follow the bare stem of another verb, agree with the subject and never take ने.

items.q: Which says “I can't hear your voice” (a man on the phone, trying)?
items.a: मैं तुम्हारी आवाज़ नहीं सुन पा रहा हूँ ।
wrong: मैं तुम्हारी आवाज़ नहीं सुन सक रहा हूँ ।
सकना is never used in the continuous. पाना can be: सुन पा रहा हूँ.
मैं तुम्हारी आवाज़ नहीं सुनकर पा रहा हूँ ।
पाना follows the bare stem (सुन), not the conjunctive participle.
items.why: पाना “manage to” can be continuous, सकना cannot.
items.say: मैं तुम्हारी आवाज़ नहीं सुन पा रहा हूँ ।
items.en: I[0] {am not managing}[3+5+6+7] to hear[4] your[1] voice[2].

items.q: Fill the gap: “I have already seen this film. (a man speaking)”
items.say: मैं यह फ़िल्म देख चुका हूँ ।
items.en: I[0] {have already seen}[3+4+5] this[1] film[2]. (a man speaking)
wrong: चुकी
चुकी is feminine. The speaker is a man.
चुके
चुके is plural. मैं takes the singular.
चुकया
Not a word. The perfective of चुकना is चुका, with no -y-.
items.why: सकना “can”, पाना “manage to” and चुकना “have already” follow the bare stem of another verb, agree with the subject and never take ने.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Pinki has already written the letter.”
items.say: पिंकी चिट्ठी लिख चुकी है ।
wrong: पिंकी ने
चुकना never takes ने, even after a transitive stem like लिख.
पिंकी को
को does not mark the subject of चुकना. The subject stays in the plain form.
items.why: सकना “can”, पाना “manage to” and चुकना “have already” follow the bare stem of another verb, agree with the subject and never take ने.

items.q: Answer “No, he hasn't read it yet.”
items.a: नहीं, उसने अभी पत्र नहीं पढ़ा है ।
wrong: नहीं, वह अभी पत्र नहीं पढ़ चुका है ।
The book notes that चुकना is rarely used in the negative. The usual reply drops it and uses the plain perfective, with ने.
नहीं, उसने अभी पत्र नहीं पढ़ चुका है ।
चुकना never takes ने, and in the negative the plain perfective is used instead: उसने … नहीं पढ़ा है.
items.why: चुकना is rarely negative. “Not yet” uses the plain perfective.
items.hi: क्या राज पत्र पढ़ चुका है ?
items.say: नहीं, उसने अभी पत्र नहीं पढ़ा है ।
items.en: No[0], he[1] {hasn't}[4+6] read[5] the letter[3] yet[2].

items.q: Which sentence is correct?
wrong: मैं हिन्दी सकता हूँ ।
सकना cannot stand alone. It always follows a verb stem, बोल सकता.
मैं हिन्दी बोलना सकता हूँ ।
सकना follows the bare stem, not the infinitive, बोल सकता.
items.why: सकना, पाना and चुकना never stand alone: the stem of the main verb comes first.
items.say: मैं हिन्दी बोल सकता हूँ ।

items.q: Fill the gap: “The milkman will have already come by now.”
items.say: दूधवाला अब तक आ चुका होगा ।
wrong: चुकी
चुकी is feminine. दूधवाला is a man.
चुके
चुके is plural. दूधवाला is one man.
items.why: चुका होगा “will have already …, must have already …”.

lessons.title: सो गया, खा लिया, दे दिया
lessons.desc: Compound verbs with जाना, लेना, देना

items.q: Fill the gap: “The little child fell asleep quickly.”
items.say: छोटा बच्चा जल्दी सो गया ।
wrong: गई
गई is feminine. बच्चा is masculine.
गए
गए is plural. छोटा बच्चा is one child.
items.why: जाना as the second verb gives completeness or a change of state (सो जाना, बदल जाना, हो जाना).

items.q: Fill the gap: “Mohan drank up all the milk.”
items.say: मोहन सारा दूध पी गया ।
wrong: मोहन ने
पी जाना ends in जाना, which is intransitive, so there is no ने.
मोहन को
को does not mark the subject. The subject of पी जाना stays in the plain form.
items.why: A compound verb takes ने only when both verbs are ने verbs (बेच दिया, खा लिया). With जाना as the second verb there is no ने.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Sita washed all the clothes.”
items.say: सीता ने सारे कपड़े धो लिए ।
wrong: ली
ली would agree with सीता. With ने the verb agrees with कपड़े, masculine plural.
लिया
लिया is singular. कपड़े is plural.
items.why: A compound verb takes ने only when both verbs are ने verbs (बेच दिया, खा लिया). With जाना as the second verb there is no ने.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Raj broke that old glass.”
items.say: राज ने वह पुराना गिलास तोड़ दिया ।
wrong: राज
In तोड़ देना both verbs are ने verbs, so the doer takes ने.
राज को
को does not mark the doer. The doer of a transitive perfective takes ने.
items.why: A compound verb takes ने only when both verbs are ने verbs (बेच दिया, खा लिया). With जाना as the second verb there is no ने.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Sita made tea for me.”
items.hi: सीता ने मेरे लिए चाय बना ___ ।
items.say: सीता ने मेरे लिए चाय बना दी ।
wrong: दिया
दिया is masculine. With ने the verb agrees with चाय, feminine.
दीं is plural. चाय is singular.
items.why: लेना as the second verb turns the benefit towards the doer, देना away from the doer. A compound verb takes ने only when both verbs are ने verbs (बेच दिया, खा लिया). With जाना as the second verb there is no ने.

items.q: Grandma can't read. Ask Raj to read her letter out to her.
items.a: राज, दादी का पत्र पढ़कर सुना दो ।
wrong: राज, दादी का पत्र पढ़ लो ।
With लेना the benefit flows towards the doer, “read it to yourself”. Reading aloud to someone is पढ़कर सुनाना, with देना because it is done for her.
राज, दादी का पत्र पढ़कर दो ।
पढ़कर दो is two actions, “read it and then hand it over”, not reading it out.
items.why: लेना as the second verb turns the benefit towards the doer, देना away from the doer.
items.say: राज, दादी का पत्र पढ़कर सुना दो ।

items.q: Fill the gap: “My key got lost.”
items.say: मेरी चाबी खो गई ।
wrong: दी
खो देना is transitive, “to lose something”, and needs a doer with ने (मैंने चाबी खो दी). Here चाबी itself is the subject.
गया
गया is masculine. चाबी is feminine.
items.why: With verbs that can be transitive or intransitive (खोना, बदलना), जाना as the second verb makes the use intransitive.

items.q: Fill the gap: “This town has changed a lot.”
items.say: यह शहर बहुत बदल गया है ।
wrong: दिया
बदल देना is transitive, “to change something”, and needs a doer with ने. Here the town itself has changed.
गई
गई is feminine. शहर is masculine.
items.why: With verbs that can be transitive or intransitive (खोना, बदलना), जाना as the second verb makes the use intransitive.

items.q: Fill the gap: “The weather has turned cold.”
items.say: मौसम ठंडा हो गया है ।
wrong: गई
गई is feminine. मौसम is masculine.
गए
गए is plural. मौसम is singular.
items.why: जाना as the second verb gives completeness or a change of state (सो जाना, बदल जाना, हो जाना).

items.q: Fill the gap: “Oh, the bus has arrived!”
items.say: अरे, बस आ गई है !
wrong: गया
गया is masculine. बस is feminine.
गईं
गईं is plural, and before है there is no nasal. It is one bus.
items.why: जाना as the second verb gives completeness or a change of state (सो जाना, बदल जाना, हो जाना).

items.q: Which sentence is more natural?
items.a: आज राज ने अख़बार नहीं पढ़ा ।
wrong: आज राज ने अख़बार नहीं पढ़ लिया ।
Compound verbs express manner, so they are much less used in the negative: an action that hasn't happened has no manner.
आज राज ने अख़बार नहीं पढ़ दिया ।
पढ़ देना is “read out for someone”, and a compound is out of place in a plain negative statement anyway.
items.why: Compound verbs are mostly used with completed actions and commands, much less with negatives.
items.say: आज राज ने अख़बार नहीं पढ़ा ।

lessons.title: लौट आना, ले जाना
lessons.desc: Verbs in combination, and चला जाना

items.q: Fill the gap: “Father came back home in the evening.”
items.hi: पिता जी शाम को घर लौट ___ ।
items.say: पिता जी शाम को घर लौट आए ।
wrong: गए
लौट गए is “went back”. The cue is “came back”.
आया
आया is singular. पिता जी takes the respectful plural.
items.why: In लौट आना, ले जाना, निकल आना both verbs keep their meaning. The last verb is आना or जाना, so there is no ने.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Please take the children to school.”
items.say: बच्चों को स्कूल ले जाइए ।
wrong: आइए
ले आइए is “bring (here)”. Taking them away to school is ले जाइए.
गए
गए is the perfective, “took”. The cue is a command.
items.why: In लौट आना, ले जाना, निकल आना both verbs keep their meaning. The last verb is आना or जाना, so there is no ने.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Sita brought a lot of luggage with her.”
items.hi: ___ अपने साथ बहुत सामान ले आई ।
items.say: सीता अपने साथ बहुत सामान ले आई ।
items.en: Sita[0] brought[5+6] {a lot of}[3] luggage[4] {with her}[1+2].
wrong: सीता ने
ले आना ends in आना, so there is no ने, though लेना is transitive.
सीता को
को does not mark the subject. The subject of ले आना stays in the plain form.
items.why: In लौट आना, ले जाना, निकल आना both verbs keep their meaning. The last verb is आना or जाना, so there is no ने.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Sangeeta got angry with me and went away.”
items.say: मुझसे नाराज़ होकर संगीता चली गई ।
items.en: Sangeeta[3] {got angry}[1+2] with me[0] and {went away}[4+5].
wrong: चला
चला is masculine. In चला जाना the first verb is a participle and agrees with the subject.
चले
चले is plural. संगीता, spoken of plainly, takes चली.
items.why: In चला जाना “to go away” चला is a participle, not a stem, so it agrees with the subject: संगीता चली गई.

items.q: Fill the gap: “The moon came out at night.”
items.say: रात को चाँद निकल आया ।
wrong: आई
आई is feminine. चाँद is masculine.
आए
आए is plural. There is one moon.
items.why: In लौट आना, ले जाना, निकल आना both verbs keep their meaning. The last verb is आना or जाना, so there is no ने.

items.q: What is the difference between ले आना and ले जाना?
wrong: ले आना “take away”, ले जाना “bring”
It is the other way round: आना is towards the speaker, जाना away.
ले आना takes ने, ले जाना does not
Neither takes ने. The last verb, आना or जाना, is intransitive.
items.why: In लौट आना, ले जाना, निकल आना both verbs keep their meaning. The last verb is आना or जाना, so there is no ने.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
wrong: Usha brought her books.
That would be ले आई. ले गई is “took away”.
Usha bought her books.
“Bought” would be ख़रीदीं. ले गई is “took away”.
items.why: In लौट आना, ले जाना, निकल आना both verbs keep their meaning. The last verb is आना or जाना, so there is no ने.

wrong: नहाना
नहाना is the infinitive. The first action is stem + कर, नहाकर.
मैंने
आना is intransitive, so मैं takes no ने.
नहानाकर
Not a word. कर goes on the bare stem: नहाकर.

items.en: Sita[0] sat[4] in[3] the garden[2] and read[6] the newspaper[5].
wrong: पढ़ी
पढ़ी would agree with सीता. With ने the verb agrees with अख़बार, masculine.
बैठा
बैठा is a participle, “seated”. The first action is the conjunctive participle बैठकर.
बैठनाकर
Not a word. कर goes on the bare stem: बैठकर.
सकता
सकता is singular. हम takes सकते.
हमने
सकना never takes ने.
सकया
Not a word. The perfective of सकना is सका, with no -y-, and here the present सकते is needed.
ने
पाना after a verb stem never takes ने, and पहुँचना is intransitive anyway.
पाई
पाई is feminine. पाना agrees with the subject, राज.
पाआ
Not a word. After a vowel stem the masculine singular inserts -y-: पाया.
चुका
चुका is singular. The guests are plural (हैं).
पहुँचकर
चुकना follows the bare stem, पहुँच चुके.
चुकया
Not a word. The perfective of चुकना is चुका, चुके, चुकी.
ने
सो जाना is intransitive, so there is no ने.
बजा
“At” a time takes the oblique बजे.
दी
दी would agree with दादी. With ने the verb agrees with सेब, masculine plural here.
दीं is feminine plural. सेब is masculine.
आओ
ले आओ is “bring”. “Take away” is ले जाओ.
तुम्हारे
The subject's own company is अपने साथ, not तुम्हारे साथ.

items.en: Sangeeta[0] came[4+5] out[3] of[2] the house[1].
wrong: ने
निकल आना ends in आना, so there is no ने.
आया
आया is masculine. Sangeeta is a woman.
बजा
बजा goes with one o'clock (एक बजा है). Two and upwards take बजे हैं.
पौने
पौने पाँच is a quarter to five.
बजने
छह बजने में दस मिनट would be “ten to six”.
बजा
बजा goes with one o'clock (एक बजा है). Minutes past the hour use बजकर.
बजेकर
Not a word. कर goes on the bare stem of बजना, बजकर.
items.order: The hour comes first: छह बजकर दस मिनट is ten past six, दस बजकर छह मिनट would be six minutes past ten.

wrong: लिया
लिया is singular. सारे आम is plural.
बच्चे
Before ने the noun is oblique, बच्चों.

lessons.title: What does it mean?
lessons.desc: Read a sentence, pick the translation

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
wrong: Raj came late by mistake.
That is the opposite. जान-बूझकर is “deliberately”.
Raj knew he would come late.
जान-बूझकर is one adverb, “deliberately”, not a separate verb “knew”.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: पिंकी को छोड़कर सब बच्चे सो गए ।
items.a: All the children except Pinki went to sleep.
wrong: Only Pinki went to sleep.
It is the other way round: everyone except Pinki went to sleep.
All the children went to sleep near Pinki.
को छोड़कर means “except”, not “near” (के पास).

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.a: Will you come today or tomorrow?
wrong: Will you come today and tomorrow?
कि between two simple alternatives in a question means “or”, not “and”.
Did you come today or yesterday?
आओगे is future, so कल here is “tomorrow”.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: मेरा छोटा भाई तीसरे पहर सो जाता है ।
items.a: My little brother goes to sleep in the afternoon.
wrong: My little brother sleeps for three hours.
पहर is a watch of about three hours, but तीसरे पहर is a phrase, “in the afternoon”.
My little brother went to sleep at three.
सो जाता है is the present habitual, and “at three” would be तीन बजे.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
wrong: He couldn't understand what you said.
That would be नहीं समझ पाया or नहीं समझ सका.
He understood you and left.
समझ गया is one compound verb, “realized”. There is no leaving.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: सीता दस बजकर बीस मिनट पर घर से निकली ।
items.a: Sita left home at twenty past ten.
wrong: Sita left home at twenty to ten.
That would be दस बजने में बीस मिनट पर.
Sita left home at half past ten.
That would be साढ़े दस बजे.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: आप अब घर जा सकते हैं ।
wrong: You managed to go home.
That would be पाना in the past, जा पाए.
You have already gone home.
That would be चुकना, जा चुके हैं.

items.q: Does the conjunctive participle decide whether the main verb takes ने?
items.a: No, only the main verb decides about ने
wrong: Yes, a transitive conjunctive participle brings ने
No. In पिंकी दूध पीकर सो गई there is no ने, because सो जाना is intransitive.
Yes, an intransitive conjunctive participle removes ने
No. In सीता ने बाज़ार जाकर साड़ी ख़रीदी the doer keeps ने.
items.why: The conjunctive participle does not affect the main clause: whether the doer takes ने depends only on the main verb.

items.q: After a verb stem, which of सकना, पाना and चुकना take ने?
wrong: All three, after a transitive stem
They never take ने. Compare सीता वह चिट्ठी नहीं पढ़ सकी.
Only the one meaning “have already”
चुकना doesn't take ने either: पिंकी चिट्ठी लिख चुकी है.
items.why: सकना “can”, पाना “manage to” and चुकना “have already” follow the bare stem of another verb, agree with the subject and never take ने.

items.q: Which of these is never used in the continuous?
wrong: पाना
पाना can be, as in सुन पा रहा हूँ.
होना
होना has a continuous, हो रहा है.
items.why: सकना is never continuous. To say “I can't … (right now)” use पाना, as in नहीं सुन पा रहा हूँ.

items.q: When does a compound verb take ने?
items.a: When both verbs are ने verbs (बेच दिया)
wrong: Whenever the main verb is transitive (पी गया)
Not enough. पी गया has no ने, because जाना is intransitive.
Whenever the second verb is transitive (हँस दी)
Not enough. हँसना is intransitive, so वह हँस दी has no ने.
items.why: A compound verb takes ने only when both verbs are ने verbs (बेच दिया, खा लिया). With जाना as the second verb there is no ने.

items.q: What does लेना suggest as the second verb of a compound?
items.a: The benefit flows towards the doer
wrong: The benefit flows away from the doer
That is देना.
The action is already finished
That is चुकना.
items.why: लेना as the second verb turns the benefit towards the doer, देना away from the doer.

items.q: What does जाना add as the second verb of a compound?
items.a: Completeness or a change of state
wrong: Motion away from the speaker
In a compound जाना loses that meaning. It keeps it only in combinations such as लौट जाना.
Ability
That is सकना.
items.why: जाना as the second verb gives completeness or a change of state (सो जाना, बदल जाना, हो जाना).

items.q: Why are compound verbs rarely used in negative sentences?
items.a: They express manner, and an action that didn't happen has no manner
wrong: They always take ने
They don't. सो गया has no ने.
They cannot be used in the past
They are mostly used with completed actions, as in खा लिया.
items.why: Compound verbs are mostly used with completed actions and commands, much less with negatives, continuous tenses and conjunctive participles.

items.q: How do लौट आना and चला जाना differ in form?
items.a: लौट is a bare stem, चला a participle that agrees (चली गई)
wrong: Both लौट and चला are bare stems
चला agrees with the subject, as in संगीता चली गई.
Both लौट and चला are participles that agree
लौट never changes, as in सीता लौट आई, वे लौट आए.
items.why: In लौट आना the first verb is a stem. In चला जाना, चला आना it is a participle that agrees with the subject.
